gloss: go out as a host, wage war; serve; host, army; warfare, service; (Aramaic) will, wish
summary: צָבָא is a host: a body of men mustered and sent out under a commander, as Israel was counted “every one going out in the host” and set out from Sinai “by their hosts” (Num 1:3; 10:14, 28). It is also what the host does, the going out to war, and so any appointed service or hard term of duty, the Levites’ “service” at the tent and man’s “hard service” on earth (Num 4:3, 23; Job 7:1). The sun, moon and stars are “the host of the heavens”, and so are Yahweh’s angels who stand by his throne and do his will (Deu 4:19; 1Ki 22:19; Psa 103:21); Yahweh of hosts (יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת) is the commander of them all and of Israel’s ranks (1Sa 17:45). The verb is to go out as a host, to wage war or to serve; Sabaic ḍbʾ “wage war” and Punic ṣbʾ “army” are the same word. Biblical Aramaic צְבָא “wish, will” has the same spelling but its cognates show a different older root.

words.gloss: host, army; war, campaign; service, term of duty; the host of the heavens
words.summary: Nearly five hundred uses: half of them in the title יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת, most of the rest of an army or of the host of the heavens. The noun names the body that is mustered, the campaign it goes on, and any service done under orders.

senses.definition: A body of men mustered by count and sent out under a commander (שַׂר צָבָא); in Numbers, each tribe’s fighting men under its prince, and Israel as a whole “by their hosts”.

evidence.note: “Every one going out in the צָבָא in Israel, you shall count them לְצִבְאֹתָם, by their hosts”: the host is the men of twenty and up, mustered by count.
Israel camps each man by his camp and by his banner, לְצִבְאֹתָם.
Judah’s banner camps on the east by their hosts, “and his צָבָא and their counted ones, 74,600”.
At the trumpets’ signal the banner of Judah’s camp sets out first לְצִבְאֹתָם, “and over his צָבָא was Nahshon son of Amminadab”: each tribe’s host under its prince.
So the host of each tribe in turn, with its prince over it.
“These were the setting-outs of the sons of Israel לְצִבְאֹתָם, and they set out.”
Phicol, שַׂר צְבָאוֹ, the commander of Abimelech’s host.
Sisera, the commander of Jabin’s host.
Abner, the commander of Saul’s host.
Israel makes Omri, שַׂר צָבָא, king in the camp.
Yahweh’s wrath on all the nations “and on all their צְבָאָם”.
“The women who bring the news are a great צָבָא”: a host of women.

senses.definition: Israel brought out of Egypt in their ranks, called Yahweh’s own hosts.

evidence.note: “I will bring out צִבְאֹתַי, my people the sons of Israel, from the land of Egypt”: Yahweh’s hosts are his people.
“On that very day all צִבְאוֹת יְהוָה went out from the land of Egypt.”
“Bring out the sons of Israel … עַל צִבְאֹתָם.”
The journeys of Israel who went out of Egypt לְצִבְאֹתָם.

senses.gloss: war, warfare; going out to war
senses.definition: The going out of a host: a campaign or war, chiefly in the phrase יֹצֵא צָבָא “one going out to war” and “to go up to the צָבָא”.

evidence.note: A newly married man “shall not go out בַּצָּבָא”, nor be charged with any business, for a year: war duty.
“Arm men from among you לַצָּבָא, and let them be against Midian.”
A thousand from each tribe sent לַצָּבָא.
The officers “coming from the צְבָא הַמִּלְחָמָה”, the war campaign.
The congregation gathers at Shiloh “to go up against them לַצָּבָא”.
The second census: “every one going out to war in Israel”.
From Zebulun, יוֹצְאֵי צָבָא, “setting the battle in array”.
“Yahweh of hosts is mustering a צְבָא מִלְחָמָה”, a host for battle.

senses.gloss: service (of the Levites at the tent)
senses.definition: The Levites’ appointed duty in the tent of meeting, entered at a fixed age and left at fifty: the word for a soldier’s service used of service in the sanctuary.

evidence.note: From thirty to fifty years, “every one coming לַצָּבָא, to do work in the tent of meeting”.
“Every one coming לִצְבֹא צָבָא, to serve service in the tent of meeting.”
“From fifty years he shall return from the צְבָא הָעֲבֹדָה, and serve no more.”
From twenty-five years the Levite “shall come to serve the צָבָא”.

senses.gloss: hard service, an appointed term of toil
senses.definition: A set term of hardship under another’s orders, like a soldier’s or a hired man’s: man’s life on earth, Jerusalem’s time of punishment.

evidence.note: “Is there not a צָבָא for man on earth, and are not his days like the days of a hired man?”: set beside the hireling’s days.
“If a man dies, shall he live again? All the days of my צָבָא I would wait, until my relief (חֲלִיפָה) comes”: a term of duty that ends in being relieved.
“Speak to the heart of Jerusalem and call to her that her צָבָא is fulfilled, that her iniquity is accepted as paid”: her term of punishment is done.
“The word was true, וְצָבָא גָדוֹל”: a great conflict (or a long, hard term) foretold.

senses.gloss: the host of the heavens: stars; angels
senses.definition: All that fills the heavens as an ordered host under its maker: the sun, moon and stars, which Yahweh brings out by number and calls by name, and the angels who stand by his throne and do his word.

evidence.note: “The heavens and the earth were finished, וְכָל צְבָאָם”: all that fills them.
“The sun and the moon and the stars, all צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם.”
“Who created these? He who brings out צְבָאָם by number; he calls them all by name”: the stars as a mustered host.
“As צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם cannot be numbered … so I will multiply the seed of David.”
By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, “and all צְבָאָם by the breath of his mouth”.
“My hands stretched out the heavens, and all צְבָאָם I commanded.”
“I saw Yahweh sitting on his throne, and all צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם standing by him on his right and on his left”: the angels. Also 2Ch 18:18.
“Bless Yahweh, his angels … bless Yahweh, all צְבָאָיו, his ministers who do his will”: the hosts set beside the angels.
“Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all צְבָאָיו.”
“I am שַׂר צְבָא יְהוָה”: the commander of Yahweh’s host appears to Joshua.
You made the heavens “and all צְבָאָם … and צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם bow down to you”.

senses.gloss: the host of the heavens as worshipped
senses.definition: Sun, moon and stars bowed to and burned incense to, which the law forbade and Israel’s kings practised.

evidence.note: One who “served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם, which I have not commanded”.
Israel “bowed down to all the host of the heavens and served Baal”.
Manasseh. Also 21:5.
Josiah puts down those who burned incense “to Baal, to the sun and the moon and the constellations, and all the host of the heavens”.
Bones spread before the sun and moon and all the host of the heavens, “which they loved and served”.
Incense burned on the roofs to all the host of the heavens.
Those who bow down on the roofs לִצְבָא הַשָּׁמָיִם.

senses.gloss: the host of the heights: ruling powers (in prophecy)
senses.definition: In prophecy, the host of the heavens set beside the kings of the earth and cast down to the ground: the powers that rule a people.

evidence.note: Yahweh will punish “צְבָא הַמָּרוֹם in the height, and the kings of the earth on the earth”: in parallel.
“All צְבָא הַשָּׁמַיִם will rot away and the heavens be rolled up like a scroll”, in judgment on the nations and their armies (34:2) and on Edom (34:5).

The horn grew great “to צְבָא הַשָּׁמָיִם, and cast down to the ground some of the host and of the stars, and trampled them”; explained in 8:24: “he shall destroy mighty men and the people of the holy ones”.
It magnifies itself against שַׂר הַצָּבָא; “the sanctuary and the host” are trampled.

senses.definition: In the title יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת, יְהוָה אֱלֹהֵי צְבָאוֹת, “Yahweh (God) of hosts”: Yahweh as commander of every host, Israel’s ranks and the hosts of heaven. It first appears at Shiloh (1Sa 1:3) and fills the prophets after the exile.

evidence.note: “I come to you in the name of יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת, the God of the ranks (מַעַרְכוֹת) of Israel, whom you have defied”: the hosts include Israel’s battle lines.
“Who is this King of glory? יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת, he is the King of glory”, after “Yahweh mighty in battle” (24:8).
The first use: Elkanah goes up to worship and sacrifice to Yahweh of hosts at Shiloh.
“The ark of the covenant of Yahweh of hosts, who sits above the cherubim.”
“David went on and became great, and Yahweh God of hosts was with him.”
“Holy, holy, holy is יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת; the whole earth is full of his glory”: so the seraphim, his heavenly host, call him.
“Unless Yahweh of hosts had left us a remnant, we would have been like Sodom.” Quoted in Rom 9:29.
“Yahweh of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.”
He who forms the mountains and creates the wind … “Yahweh God of hosts is his name”.
“Yahweh, the King of Israel and his redeemer, Yahweh of hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and besides me there is no God.”
“Not by army (חַיִל) nor by power, but by my spirit, says Yahweh of hosts.”
“I am a great King, says Yahweh of hosts, and my name is feared among the nations.”
“Kings of armies (מַלְכֵי צְבָאוֹת) flee, they flee”: the plural of human armies.
“Unless κύριος σαβαὼθ had left us a seed, we would have become like Sodom”: Isa 1:9, the Hebrew plural kept in the Greek.
The cries of the defrauded reapers “have entered into the ears of κυρίου σαβαώθ”.
“[in LXX for צְבָאוֹת, chiefly in Isaiah] … Sabaoth, i.e. hosts or armies: Ro 9:29 (LXX), Ja 5:4.”

evidence.locator: Isa.1.9 and Isa.6.3, צְבָאוֹת → σαβαώθ; σαβαώθ renders צָבָא ×52
2Sa.7.8, יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת → κύριος παντοκράτωρ; παντοκράτωρ renders צָבָא ×116

evidence.note: “I will be a father to you … says κύριος παντοκράτωρ”: the promise to David (2Sa 7:8, 14), where the Hebrew has Yahweh of hosts.
“Holy, holy, holy, κύριος ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ”: the seraphim’s cry of Isa 6:3.

evidence.locator: Num.10.14, צְבָאוֹ → δυνάμει; Num.1.3; 2Ch.18.18 (the host of the heavens); δύναμις renders צָבָא ×88

evidence.note: “The stars will fall from heaven, and αἱ δυνάμεις τῶν οὐρανῶν will be shaken”: the language of Isa 34:4, “all the host of the heavens will rot away”.

evidence.locator: Zep.1.5, לִצְבָא הַשָּׁמָיִם → τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ; 2Sa.8.16; στρατιά renders צָבָא ×10

evidence.note: Stephen: “God turned and gave them up to serve τῇ στρατιᾷ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ”, the host of heaven Israel worshipped.
“A multitude στρατιᾶς οὐρανίου praising God”: the angels as the heavenly host.
“Every priest stands daily λειτουργῶν”: the sanctuary service.

parallels.note: Yahweh’s angels, set beside his hosts.
“The kings of the earth” beside “the host of the height”.
The hired man’s days, beside man’s צָבָא on earth.
“Service”: the Levites’ צָבָא is to serve the עֲבֹדָה of the tent.

phrases.gloss: one going out to war; of age for war
by their hosts, in their ranks

words.gloss: go out as a host: wage war; serve (at the tent); (hiphil) muster
words.summary: Fourteen uses, the verb of the noun: to do what a host does, go out against an enemy or serve one’s appointed duty.

stems.gloss: wage war, fight; serve (at the tent)

senses.gloss: go out to war, wage war (against, עַל)
senses.definition: To go out as a host against an enemy.

evidence.note: “They went to war (וַיִּצְבְּאוּ) against Midian, as Yahweh commanded Moses, and killed every male.”
The spoil divided from “the men הַצֹּבְאִים”, who had gone to war.
“The multitude of all the nations הַצֹּבְאִים against Ariel, and all who war against her (צֹבֶיהָ, spelled without א) … against Mount Zion.”
“So Yahweh of hosts will come down לִצְבֹּא upon Mount Zion and upon its hill”, as a lion over its prey; 31:5, so he will defend Jerusalem.
The plague on “all the peoples who went to war (צָבְאוּ) against Jerusalem”.

senses.definition: To do appointed service at the sanctuary: the Levites from their coming of age, and the women who served at the entrance of the tent.

evidence.note: “Every one coming לִצְבֹא צָבָא, to serve the service in the tent of meeting.”
The Levite from twenty-five years “shall come לִצְבֹא צָבָא in the service of the tent of meeting”.
The basin made from the mirrors of “the women הַצֹּבְאֹת who served (צָבְאוּ) at the entrance of the tent of meeting”.
Eli’s sons lay with “the women הַצֹּבְאוֹת at the entrance of the tent of meeting”.

senses.definition: To make men go out as a host: the scribe of the army’s commander who mustered the people of the land.

evidence.note: “The scribe of the commander of the host, הַמַּצְבִּא, who mustered the people of the land.”

words.summary: Daniel’s Aramaic verb “wish, will”. It shares the spelling צבא but not the meaning: its cognates (Akkadian ṣabû, Arabic ṣabā, with ṣ) belong to a root ending in a weak letter, ṣbw/ṣby, and the Aramaic spelling with א is the usual merging of such verbs in Aramaic. Its tie to the root “host” is therefore not shown; it stays in this entry by its spelling.

senses.gloss: will, wish (of the one who rules)
senses.definition: To will or choose freely, as a ruler does: chiefly of the Most High, who gives the kingdom “to whom he wills”; and of Nebuchadnezzar’s power, which was given him.

evidence.note: “That the living may know that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men, and gives it to whom he wills (יִצְבֵּא), and sets over it the lowest of men.” Also 4:22, 29.
“He does according to his will (כְמִצְבְּיֵהּ) in the host of heaven (חֵיל שְׁמַיָּא) and among the inhabitants of the earth, and none can stay his hand.”
Of Nebuchadnezzar, from the greatness God gave him: “whom he willed (צָבֵא) he killed, and whom he willed he kept alive; whom he willed he raised, and whom he willed he put down.”
Until he knew “that the Most High God rules in the kingdom of men and sets over it whom he wills”.
“Then I wished (צְבִית) to know the truth about the fourth beast.”

evidence.locator: Dan.4.14, יִצְבֵּא → θέλῃ; Dan.7.19, צְבִית → ἤθελον

evidence.note: “He has mercy on whom he wills (θέλει), and whom he wills he hardens”: the same pattern as Dan 5:19, said of God.
“Not as I will (θέλω), but as you will.”

words.summary: One use, the noun of the Aramaic verb “will”: what is purposed, a matter. Jewish Aramaic צְבוּ is “will, desire”, and the Peshitta’s ܨܒܘܬܐ “thing, matter” is from the same root. Like the verb, it is tied to צבא only by its spelling.

senses.definition: A purpose or matter: in Dan 6:18, that nothing purposed concerning Daniel might be changed.

evidence.note: The stone is sealed with the king’s signet and his lords’, “that צְבוּ might not be changed concerning Daniel”: the purpose, the matter.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܨܒܐ (ṣbā), its usual word for θέλω “will, wish”: the same word as Daniel’s צְבָא.

senses.definition: To will or wish: of the leper’s plea and Jesus’ answer, and of Jesus yielding his will to the Father’s.

evidence.note: “Lord, if you will (ܨܒܐ), you can make me clean” … “I will (ܨܒܐ ܐܢܐ); be clean.”
“Not as I will, but as you will.”
Joseph, “not willing to make her a public example”.
Having tasted the vinegar mixed with gall, “he would not drink”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܨܒܝܢܐ (ṣebyānā), the noun of ܨܒܐ: will, for θέλημα.

senses.definition: What one wills: above all the Father’s will, which Jesus came to do.

evidence.note: “Your kingdom come; your will (ܨܒܝܢܟ) be done, as in heaven, so on earth.”
“I came down from heaven not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me.” Also 6:39–40.
“Your will be done.”
Only he who does the will of my Father enters the kingdom.
“My food is to do the will of him who sent me.”
Psa 40:8: “I have come to do your will, O God”; “by that will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all”.

words.summary: The Peshitta’s ܨܒܐܘܬ (ṣbāʾōt), the Hebrew plural kept as it is in the title “Lord of hosts” where the Greek has σαβαώθ.

senses.definition: In the title ܡܪܝܐ ܨܒܐܘܬ, “Lord of hosts”: יְהוָה צְבָאוֹת.

evidence.note: Isa 1:9: “Unless the Lord of hosts had left us a seed.”
The reapers’ cries have entered the ears of the Lord of hosts.

cognates.gloss: (Sabaic) wage war, fight; ḍbʾ, pl. ḍbʾt battle, war; fighters
cognates.note: Old South Arabian keeps the older ḍ (ṣ́) apart from ṣ, so this is the sound behind צ in צָבָא. The inscriptions pair it with sbʾ “go on campaign” and gzw “raid”, and speak of “the armies he sent to wage war (ldbʾ) against them”: the same going out of a host as the Hebrew verb. Biella compares Ethiopic ḍabʾa and Hebrew ṣābāʾ.

evidence.note: “v … WAGE WAR, FIGHT … [Eth ḍabʾa, Heb ṣabaʾ id] … J577/14: and as for the armies he sent to wage war against them …; s ḍbʾ … BATTLE, ENGAGEMENT, FIGHT; WAR … p ḍbʾt … FIGHTERS, SOLDIERS (?)”. Read from the OCR text layer.

cognates.note: A Punic dedication made “on behalf of his father and the army”, and the Neo-Punic of Plautus “our militia surrounded Mycne”: the noun in the same sense.

evidence.note: “[Heb. ṣābāʾ] n.m. ARMY, MILITIA. CIS i 197 (Pu) … vowed on behalf of his father and the army …; Poen. (NPu) Sab siben Mycne, ‘Our militia surrounded Mycne’”. Read from the text layer.

cognates.gloss: people; troops, soldiers, army; workers, gang of workmen
cognates.note: A body of men raised for war or for labour: both the army and the work-gang, as the Hebrew צָבָא is both the host and its appointed service. Akkadian does not keep ṣ and ṣ́ apart.

evidence.note: army; man; men; people; soldiers; troops; workers (×6785).

cognates.gloss: cleave to the ground and hide, lie in wait (for game or prey)
cognates.note: The consonants answer to Sabaic ḍbʾ, but the Arabic sense is lying hidden in ambush, not going out as a host; a hunter’s or a raider’s lying in wait may be the bridge, but nothing in Lane shows it.

evidence.note: “He clave to the ground … and hid, or concealed, himself … in a covert of trees, or in a hollow in the ground, to deceive, or circumvent, the game, or prey”; مَضْبَأٌ “a place where one conceals himself … to deceive … the game”.

cognates.gloss: wish (for), desire, request; ṣibûtu wish, desire, purpose
cognates.note: The Aramaic verb צְבָא “will” and its noun צְבוּ “purpose” answer to this verb and its noun ṣibûtu, “wish, purpose, what is needed”.

evidence.note: desire; request; wish (for) (×53).
desire; interest; objective; plan; purpose; request; what is needed; wish (×195).

cognates.gloss: incline (to); yearn, desire; (II, III) incline, lower
cognates.note: Lane’s sources derive the verb’s sense “inclined to youthful folly” from الشَّوْق “desire”, and form IV is to excite desire and make one incline; II and III are to incline the head or the spear. “Incline toward, desire” would answer to the Aramaic “will”; the Arabic is mostly of youth and its follies, so the tie is possible only. Its ṣ differs from the ḍ (ṣ́) of Sabaic ḍbʾ “wage war”: two older roots in the one spelling.

evidence.note: “He inclined to ignorant, or foolish … conduct …; from الصِّبَا, which is from الشَّوْق [i.e. ‘desire’]”; II “He inclined his head towards the ground”; III “He inclined his spear”.
“She excited his desire, and invited him, or made him to incline … so that he yearned towards her.”

cognates.gloss: (Jewish Aramaic) find pleasure in, choose, desire; צְבוּ will, desire
cognates.note: The Targums use it where the Hebrew has חָפֵץ “delight in”, בָּחַר “choose” and אָבָה “be willing”.

evidence.note: “with ב, to find pleasure in, to choose, desire. Targ. Y. Gen. XXXIV, 19 (h. text חפץ). Targ. Prov. III, 31 (h. text בחר) … Targ. Y. Deut. XXIII, 6 (h. text אבה)”.
“will, desire; willingness. Targ. Y. Lev. VIII, 15 …”

doctrine.statement: The hosts Yahweh commands are of three kinds in scripture: Israel, whom he calls “my hosts, my people” when he brings them out of Egypt (Exo 7:4; 12:41), and whose battle lines are his (1Sa 17:45); the stars, which he brings out by number and calls by name (Isa 40:26; 45:12); and the angels who stand at his right hand and left and do his will (1Ki 22:19; Psa 103:20–21; Jos 5:14). So David goes against Goliath “in the name of Yahweh of hosts, the God of the ranks of Israel” (1Sa 17:45), and Zechariah hears that the house will be built “not by army nor by power, but by my spirit, says Yahweh of hosts” (Zec 4:6). Paul quotes Isaiah’s “unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed” for the remnant saved by grace (Rom 9:29; Isa 1:9), and James warns that the reapers’ cries reach “the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth” (Jas 5:4); Isaiah’s “holy, holy, holy, Yahweh of hosts” is sung in Revelation to “the Lord God Almighty” (Isa 6:3; Rev 4:8). From the verses: the title says that every power in heaven and on earth is Yahweh’s host under his command, so that his people’s safety and his purpose rest on him and not on their own strength.

Genesis closes the six days with “the heavens and the earth were finished, and all their host” (Gen 2:1), and the next verse has God resting on the seventh day; the fourth commandment rests on the same count: “in six days Yahweh made the heavens and the earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested the seventh day” (Exo 20:11). “By the word of Yahweh the heavens were made, and all their host by the breath of his mouth” (Psa 33:6); “my hands stretched out the heavens, and all their host I commanded” (Isa 45:12); the angels too are told to praise him, “for he commanded and they were created” (Psa 148:2, 5); Nehemiah’s prayer names the heavens “and all their host” among what Yahweh alone made (Neh 9:6). From the verses: the sun, moon, stars and angels were all made by Yahweh’s word and finished within the six days of creation, and none of them is a power of its own.

Moses warns Israel not to look up at “the sun and the moon and the stars, all the host of the heavens”, and be drawn away to bow down to them (Deu 4:19), and the law puts to death the one who serves them, “which I have not commanded” (Deu 17:3). Israel did it nonetheless, and it is named among the sins for which the northern kingdom was carried away (2Ki 17:16), and again in Judah under Manasseh (2Ki 21:3, 5) until Josiah put it down (2Ki 23:4–5); Jeremiah and Zephaniah condemn the incense burned to the host on the roofs (Jer 8:2; 19:13; Zep 1:5). Stephen says that God “turned and gave them up to serve the host of heaven” (Act 7:42). From the verses: the host of heaven is part of what Yahweh made and commands, and to worship it is to worship the creature in his place; God’s answer was to give the worshippers over to what they had chosen.

Isaiah sets “the host of the height in the height” beside “the kings of the earth on the earth” as those Yahweh will punish (Isa 24:21), and his “all the host of the heavens will rot away” comes in a judgment on the nations and their armies, and on Edom (Isa 34:2–5). In Daniel the horn grows great “to the host of the heavens” and casts some of the host and of the stars to the ground and tramples them (Dan 8:10), which the angel explains as destroying “mighty men and the people of the holy ones” (Dan 8:24). Jesus uses the same language, the stars falling and “the powers of the heavens” shaken, for the judgment that came on his own generation in AD 70 (Mat 24:29, 34). From the verses: in prophecy the heavens and their host stand for a nation’s ruling powers and its people of rank, and their falling for the overthrow of those powers.

Nebuchadnezzar is told, and three times, that the Most High rules in the kingdom of men “and gives it to whom he wills (יִצְבֵּא)” (Dan 4:14, 22, 29), and he confesses that God “does according to his will in the host of heaven and among the inhabitants of the earth, and none can stay his hand” (Dan 4:32). Daniel reminds Belshazzar that his father’s power to kill or keep alive “whom he willed” was given him by God, and taken away when his heart was lifted up (Dan 5:18–21). Paul says the same of God: “he has mercy on whom he wills, and whom he wills he hardens” (Rom 9:18), and Jesus tells Pilate he would have no power unless it were given from above (Joh 19:11). Jesus himself prays “not as I will, but as you will” (Mat 26:39), and came “not to do my own will, but the will of him who sent me” (Joh 6:38). From the verses: rule among men is God’s to give and to take, and the one who was given all authority is the one who yielded his own will to the Father’s.
